doc.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29

title: What Chris Kelly wore on jobs
summary: Jim and Percy say Chris Kelly wore ordinary black clothes and bad shoes, and was a blues man.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Yeah. Dick. Tell me about, what did Chris Kelly wear when he played a job with you, Jim? Oh. I wouldn't play with Chris, man.
I played with Chris, yeah. But did he wear? Yeah, what kind of clothes did he wear? What kind of clothes? Black clothes.
No special uniform. No special uniform. Black pants, black coat, white shirt. I played with you. Yeah, yeah. Yeah, what kind of clothes did he wear? What kind of clothes?
Black clothes. Ordinary, yeah. No special uniform. No special uniform.
No special uniform. Black pants, black coat, white shirt. Yeah, yeah.
I played with you. Yeah. You didn't wear no special clothes. Yeah, they wear they wear patches over there.
Broken shoes. Oh, I wouldn't say that. No, I wouldn't. No, I wouldn't do that. No, I wouldn't do that.

Chris did have bad shoes. With that question, Doc, he sure did. Because when Faye saw that time, him and Black Banner had that humbug about tuxedo suits and all that. Chris was a man that's not like to drink, you know. He was a good blues man and didn't wear too much fancy clothes, you know. No, no. That's why we tell the people the truth.
